system.text:
You are a senior software engineer on a team that maintains a production Python codebase. You
have been handed one change request. You own it from understanding the requirement to delivering
code that a reviewer can approve and merge.

Your responsibilities

Understand the requirement.
- Read the request as the product team means it, not only its literal words. Work out the inputs,
  the expected outputs, the error cases and the edge cases it implies.
- Where the request is ambiguous, choose the interpretation most consistent with the rest of the
  system and with what users of the feature would expect.

Understand the code before changing it.
- Read the code you are changing and the code it depends on or that depends on it, as far as it is
  available to you. Know what a function does from its code, not only from its name.
- Know who calls what you change. Keep public interfaces, data formats and behaviour that other code
  relies on intact unless the request asks you to change them.

Make the change correctly.
- Correctness comes first: the new behaviour must be right for every input the request implies,
  including empty, missing, zero, negative, very large and malformed values where relevant.
- Handle errors the way the codebase does: fail clearly on invalid input; never silently return
  wrong data.
- Treat money, dates, units and identifiers with care: exact arithmetic where the codebase uses it,
  explicit units, no lossy conversions.
- Don't introduce security problems: validate untrusted input and keep secrets and personal data
  out of logs and output.

Keep the codebase healthy.
- Fit in with the surrounding code: its naming, structure, typing and error handling. A reviewer
  should not be able to tell which lines are new by their style.
- Keep the change as small as the request allows, and complete: every file the change needs, none
  it doesn't. Don't refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code.
- Write code that is simple and readable; add a docstring or comment where intent is not obvious.

Check your work.
- You cannot run the code, so verify it by reading it: trace the main path and each edge case
  through your change, check every import and name you use exists, and check that everything that
  calls the code you changed still works.
- Your change will be applied to the repository and checked by tests you do not see.

What you are given
- <task>: the change request from the product team.
- <context>: material from the repository. How much varies: it may be a single file or much of the
  project. It is what you know about the codebase.

What you can and cannot do
- You cannot run code, and there is no one to ask.
- If tools are provided with this request, you may use them to look at the repository before you
  answer. If no tools are provided, you cannot open files or search: deliver the finished change in
  this reply. Tool calls, plans and requests for more files written as text are not executed, and a
  reply without code counts as no change.
- If something you need is not shown, make the most reasonable assumption consistent with what is
  shown, and implement it.

Output format (strict)
Your reply is the code change itself. Return the complete new contents of every file you create or
modify, each wrapped exactly as:
<file path="PATH">
...full file contents...
</file>
- Replace PATH with the file's real path relative to the repository root, as shown in <context> or
  <task>.
- Always the whole file, never a diff or an excerpt, and no placeholders such as "rest unchanged".
- Files you don't change are left out.
- Return nothing outside the <file> blocks: no explanations, plans or summaries before or after them.

user.label: Task (change request)
user.text:
Sellers want to see what their next payout will look like before finance runs the weekly batch.
Add `preview_payout(seller, earnings, adjustments, period_start, period_end, holds, rollover)` in a
new module `shopkit/payouts/preview.py`. It returns `(status, net_cents)`: the status and the net
amount this seller's payout would get for that period, exactly as the weekly payout would treat it.
A preview must not change anything: held amounts and balances carried between periods stay as they were.

    batch; adjustments (chargebacks, fees, corrections) and released holds are added; sellers on

    # because the new one rejected rows that the old batch paid and finance wanted to see the diff)

    valid_earnings = []
    for e in earnings:
        if e.gross_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents < 0:
            stats["rejected_negative"] += 1

                      e.gross_cents, e.refunded_cents)

        if e.refunded_cents > e.gross_cents:
            stats["rejected_overrefund"] += 1

                      e.refunded_cents, e.gross_cents)

                        " (dry run, keeping)" if dry_run_dedupe else "")

            stats["dup_in_batch"] += 1
            log.warning("INC-2377 earning %s twice in this batch%s", key, " (dry run, keeping)" if dry_run_dedupe else "")

def approve(payout: Payout, approver: str) -> None:
    if payout.status != DRAFT:
        raise ValueError(f"payout {payout.id} is {payout.status}, only drafts can be approved")
    payout.status = APPROVED
    payout.notes.append(f"approved by {approver}")


def statement_text(payout: Payout, seller: Seller) -> str:
    """Plain-text statement emailed to the seller with the payout."""
    from shopkit.money import format_money
    cur = payout.currency
    rows = [f"Payout {payout.id} for {seller.name}", f"Period {payout.period_start} to {payout.period_end}", ""]
    for l in payout.lines:
        rows.append(f"{l.order_id:<20} gross {format_money(l.gross_cents, cur):>12}  fee {format_money(l.commission_cents, cur):>10}"
                    f"  refunds {format_money(l.refunded_cents, cur):>10}  net {format_money(l.net_cents, cur):>12}")
    rows += ["", f"Held until the return window ends: {format_money(payout.held_cents, cur)}",
             f"Adjustments: {format_money(payout.adjustments_cents, cur)}",
             f"Carried from earlier periods: {format_money(payout.carried_in_cents, cur)}",
             f"Total: {format_money(payout.net_cents, cur)}"]
    if payout.status == ROLLED_OVER:
        rows.append("This amount will be added to your next payout.")
    return "\n".join(rows)

"""Holds: a seller's money for an order is held until the order's return window has passed, so a
return can still be refunded from it (migration 0023, INC-2291)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, timedelta

from shopkit.payouts.models import Earning

RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS = 30          # matches orders.returns.RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS


@dataclass
class Hold:
    seller_id: str
    order_id: str
    amount_cents: int
    release_after: date
    released: bool = False


@dataclass
class HoldBook:
    holds: dict[tuple[str, str], Hold] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def place(self, earning: Earning, net_cents: int) -> Hold:
        """Hold the net amount of an earning. Not delivered yet: held until delivery + window; the
        release date is set when delivery is known (update_delivery)."""
        key = (earning.seller_id, earning.order_id)
        release = (earning.delivered_on or date.max - timedelta(days=RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS)) + timedelta(days=RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS)
        existing = self.holds.get(key)
        if existing and not existing.released:
            existing.amount_cents += net_cents
            existing.release_after = max(existing.release_after, release) if earning.delivered_on else existing.release_after
            return existing
        hold = Hold(earning.seller_id, earning.order_id, net_cents, release)
        self.holds[key] = hold
        return hold

    def update_delivery(self, seller_id: str, order_id: str, delivered_on: date) -> None:
        hold = self.holds.get((seller_id, order_id))
        if hold and not hold.released:
            hold.release_after = delivered_on + timedelta(days=RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS)

    def releasable(self, seller_id: str, on: date) -> list[Hold]:
        return [h for h in self.holds.values() if h.seller_id == seller_id and not h.released and h.release_after <= on]

    def release(self, seller_id: str, on: date) -> int:
        """Release every hold of the seller due on `on`; returns the amount released."""
        total = 0
        for h in self.releasable(seller_id, on):
            h.released = True
            total += h.amount_cents
        return total

    def outstanding(self, seller_id: str) -> int:
        return sum(h.amount_cents for h in self.holds.values() if h.seller_id == seller_id and not h.released)

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date

ACTIVE, CLOSING, SUSPENDED, CLOSED = "active", "closing", "suspended", "closed"
DRAFT, APPROVED, SENT, FAILED, ROLLED_OVER = "draft", "approved", "sent", "failed", "rolled_over"


@dataclass
class Seller:
    id: str
    name: str
    commission_bp: int = 1500                  # 15.00%
    payout_currency: str = "USD"
    status: str = ACTIVE
    bank_account: str = ""                     # stored redacted, last 4 digits
    reserve_bp: int = 0                        # extra reserve for sellers on review (basis points of gross)
    tax_id: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Earning:
    """One order line sold by a seller."""
    seller_id: str
    order_id: str
    sku: str
    gross_cents: int
    delivered_on: date | None                  # None: not delivered yet
    refunded_cents: int = 0
    currency: str = "USD"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Adjustment:
    seller_id: str
    amount_cents: int                          # negative = deduction (chargeback, fee, correction)
    reason: str
    ref: str = ""


@dataclass
class PayoutLine:
    order_id: str
    gross_cents: int
    commission_cents: int
    refunded_cents: int
    net_cents: int


@dataclass
class Payout:
    id: str
    seller_id: str
    period_start: date
    period_end: date
    currency: str
    lines: list[PayoutLine] = field(default_factory=list)
    adjustments_cents: int = 0
    held_cents: int = 0
    reserve_cents: int = 0
    carried_in_cents: int = 0                  # rolled over from earlier periods
    status: str = DRAFT
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def gross_cents(self) -> int:
        return sum(l.gross_cents for l in self.lines)

    @property
    def commission_cents(self) -> int:
        return sum(l.commission_cents for l in self.lines)

    @property
    def net_cents(self) -> int:
        return (sum(l.net_cents for l in self.lines) + self.adjustments_cents + self.carried_in_cents
                - self.held_cents - self.reserve_cents)

"""Integer-cent arithmetic. Money is always int cents; never round through float formatting."""
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal


def apply_rate(cents: int, rate_pct: float | Decimal | str) -> int:
    """`rate_pct` percent of `cents`, rounded half-up to a whole cent (half away from zero).
    apply_rate(1999, 15) -> 300; apply_rate(-1999, 15) -> -300. Used for tax, commission, discounts."""
    value = Decimal(cents) * Decimal(str(rate_pct)) / Decimal(100)
    return int(value.quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def split_evenly(cents: int, parts: int) -> list[int]:
    """Split an amount into `parts` integer shares that sum exactly to `cents`; earlier shares get the
    leftover cents. split_evenly(1000, 3) -> [334, 333, 333]."""
    if parts < 1:
        raise ValueError("parts must be >= 1")
    base, extra = divmod(cents, parts)
    return [base + (1 if i < extra else 0) for i in range(parts)]


def safe_ratio(numerator: float, denominator: float) -> float:
    return numerator / denominator if denominator else 0.0

```python
"""Payout preview: what the seller's next payout would look like before finance runs the weekly
batch.

build_payout_batch places new holds, releases due ones and takes the seller's carried balance
from the Rollover; a preview must not change anything, so the batch's per-seller math is
replayed against a copy of the HoldBook and a plain read of the rollover.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import copy
from datetime import date, timedelta

from shopkit.config import SETTINGS
from shopkit.payouts.batching import BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP, MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS, Rollover
from shopkit.payouts.holds import RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, HoldBook
from shopkit.payouts.models import CLOSING, CLOSED, DRAFT, ROLLED_OVER, SUSPENDED, Adjustment, Earning, Payout, PayoutLine, Seller
from shopkit.utils.numbers import apply_rate


def preview_payout(seller: Seller, earnings: list[Earning], adjustments: list[Adjustment],
                   period_start: date, period_end: date, holds: HoldBook, rollover: Rollover) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """The (status, net_cents) this seller's payout would get for [period_start, period_end]
    (inclusive), computed exactly the way build_payout_batch would treat it, without changing
    anything: no holds are placed or released and the carried balance is read, not taken.

    status is DRAFT or ROLLED_OVER when the batch would make a payout, the seller's status when
    the batch would skip the seller (suspended/closed), or "no rates" when the seller is paid in
    another currency and the preview has no rate table to convert with (the batch skips those
    sellers and carries the amount over). net_cents is 0 for skipped sellers."""
    if seller.status in (SUSPENDED, CLOSED):
        return seller.status, 0

    # --- input checks, the same as the batch: reject bad earnings, keep the first of a duplicate
    # (seller, order, sku) line (INC-2377)
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    own = []
    for e in earnings:
        if e.seller_id != seller.id:
            continue
        if e.gross_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents > e.gross_cents:
            continue
        key = (e.seller_id, e.order_id, e.sku)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        own.append(e)

    # Replay the batch's hold math on a copy: the real book keeps its holds, release dates and
    # released flags exactly as they were.
    book = copy.deepcopy(holds)
```

```python
"""Payout preview: what a seller's next payout would look like before finance runs the weekly
batch (batching.py).

The batch places new holds, releases due ones and takes the seller's carried balance from the
Rollover; a preview must not change anything, so the per-seller math is replayed against a copy
of the HoldBook and a plain read of the rollover.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import copy
from datetime import date, timedelta

from shopkit.config import SETTINGS
from shopkit.payouts.batching import BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP, MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS, Rollover
from shopkit.payouts.holds import RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, HoldBook
from shopkit.payouts.models import (CLOSING, CLOSED, DRAFT, ROLLED_OVER, SUSPENDED, Adjustment,
                                    Earning, Payout, PayoutLine, Seller)
from shopkit.utils.numbers import apply_rate


def preview_payout(seller: Seller, earnings: list[Earning], adjustments: list[Adjustment],
                   period_start: date, period_end: date, holds: HoldBook, rollover: Rollover) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """The (status, net_cents) this seller's payout would get for [period_start, period_end]
    (inclusive), treated exactly the way build_payout_batch would treat it, without changing
    anything: no holds are placed or released and the carried balance is read, not taken.

    status is DRAFT or ROLLED_OVER when the batch would make a payout, the seller's own status
    when the batch would skip the seller (suspended/closed), or "no rates" when the seller is
    paid in another currency and no rate table is available (the batch skips those sellers and
    carries the amount over). Skipped sellers get net_cents 0."""
    if seller.status in (SUSPENDED, CLOSED):
        return seller.status, 0

    # --- input checks, the same as the batch: reject invalid earnings, keep the first of a
    # duplicate (seller, order, sku) line (INC-2377)
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    own = []
    for e in earnings:
        if e.seller_id != seller.id:
            continue
        if e.gross_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents > e.gross_cents:
            continue
        key = (e.seller_id, e.order_id, e.sku)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        own.append(e)

    # Replay the hold math on a copy so release dates and the released flags are decided the way
    # the batch would decide them, while the real book stays exactly as it was.
    book = copy.deepcopy(holds)

    payout = Payout(f"preview_{seller.id}_{period_end:%Y%m%d}", seller.id, period_start, period_end,
                    seller.payout_currency)
    # same window as the batch: undelivered lines plus lines delivered within a year before the
    # period start up to period_end (INC-2291)
    in_period = [e for e in own
                 if e.delivered_on is None or period_start - timedelta(days=366) <= e.delivered_on <= period_end]

    # --- lines
    held_now = 0
    for e in sorted(in_period, key=lambda e: (e.order_id, e.sku)):
        commission = apply_rate(e.gross_cents, seller.commission_bp / 100)
```

```python
    if not seller.tax_id.strip():

        if line_net > 0:
            payout.adjustments_cents -= apply_rate(line_net, BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP / 100)

    # --- minimum payout and negative balances (the rolled-over amount is carried by the batch;
    # here it is only reported)
    net = payout.net_cents
    if net < 0 or (net < MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS and seller.status != CLOSING):
        return ROLLED_OVER, net
    if seller.payout_currency != SETTINGS.default_currency:

        return "no rates", 0
    return DRAFT, net
```

weekly batch.

adjustments, reserves, carried balances, minimum payout, backup withholding, FX) and reports the
status the batch would record. A preview changes nothing: it counts the holds the batch would
place but never calls HoldBook.place/release, reads the carried balance but never calls
Rollover.take, and creates no Payout — so the real batch sees the same holds and balances."""

from datetime import date, timedelta

from shopkit.payouts.batching import BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP, FX_FEE_BP, MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS, Rollover, _commission
from shopkit.payouts.holds import RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, HoldBook

from shopkit.pricing.currency import RateTable, RateUnavailable
from shopkit.utils.numbers import apply_rate

                   rates: RateTable | None = None, settings: Settings = SETTINGS,

    skipped sellers get 0 (the batch pays them nothing); ROLLED_OVER gets the balance the batch

```python
"""Payout previews: show the seller what their next payout will look like before finance runs the
weekly batch.

Computes the same numbers build_payout_batch does for one seller (commission, return-window holds,
adjustments, reserves, carried balances, minimum payout, backup withholding, FX) and reports the
status the batch would record. A preview changes nothing: it counts the holds that would be placed
but never calls HoldBook.place/release, reads the carried balance but never calls Rollover.take,
and creates no Payout — so the real batch sees the same holds and balances."""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, timedelta

from shopkit.config import SETTINGS, Settings
from shopkit.payouts.batching import BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP, FX_FEE_BP, MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS, Rollover, _commission
from shopkit.payouts.holds import RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, HoldBook
from shopkit.payouts.models import (CLOSED, CLOSING, DRAFT, ROLLED_OVER, SUSPENDED, Adjustment,
                                    Earning, Seller)
from shopkit.pricing.currency import RateTable, RateUnavailable
from shopkit.utils.numbers import apply_rate

NO_RATES = "no rates"
RATE_UNAVAILABLE = "rate unavailable"


def preview_payout(seller: Seller, earnings: list[Earning], adjustments: list[Adjustment],
                   period_start: date, period_end: date, holds: HoldBook, rollover: Rollover,
                   rates: RateTable | None = None, settings: Settings = SETTINGS,
                   paid_lines: set[tuple[str, str, str]] | None = None,
                   seller_country: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """What the weekly batch would pay `seller` for [period_start, period_end] (both ends inclusive).

    Returns (status, net_cents): the status the batch would record for the payout (DRAFT,
    ROLLED_OVER, the skip reason "no rates" / "rate unavailable", or the seller's own status when
    suspended/closed) and the net payout in the seller's payout currency. Skipped and
    suspended/closed sellers get 0; ROLLED_OVER gets the balance the batch would carry forward.

    `holds` and `rollover` are read the way the batch reads them (which holds are releasable at
    period_end, which carried balance there is) but never written, so a preview leaves both exactly
    as they were and the real batch still processes them.

    The optional arguments mirror the batch: `rates` is required when the seller is paid in a
    currency other than the shop's, `paid_lines` are (seller, order, sku) lines already paid in an
    earlier batch, and `seller_country` drives backup withholding (US sellers without a tax ID).
    """
    # --- Input checks: same rules as the batch (negative or over-refunded lines don't become payout lines) ---
    valid = [e for e in earnings
             if e.seller_id == seller.id and e.gross_cents >= 0 and e.refunded_cents >= 0
             and e.refunded_cents <= e.gross_cents]

    # --- Deduplication, same as the batch (INC-2377): already-paid lines and duplicates in this
    #     period are not paid again. The dry-run flag is an incident switch, not the batch's
    #     behaviour, so it does not apply here.
    paid_lines = paid_lines if paid_lines is not None else frozenset()
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    deduped = []
    for e in valid:
        key = (e.seller_id, e.order_id, e.sku)
        if key in paid_lines or key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        deduped.append(e)

    in_period = [e for e in deduped
                 if e.delivered_on is None or period_start - timedelta(days=366) <= e.delivered_on <= period_end]

    # --- Lines: same commission, refund, and hold rules as the batch. The batch calls holds.place
    #     here; the preview only counts what would be held, so the book stays intact.
    gross_cents = 0
    line_nets: list[int] = []
    held_now = 0
    for e in sorted(in_period, key=lambda e: (e.order_id, e.sku)):
        commission = _commission(e.gross_cents, seller.commission_bp)
        net = e.gross_cents - commission - e.refunded_cents
        if e.refunded_cents and e.refunded_cents == e.gross_cents:
            # Fully refunded orders return the commission to the seller too (marketplace terms §7.2)
            net = 0
            commission = 0
        gross_cents += e.gross_cents
        line_nets.append(net)
        if net > 0 and (e.delivered_on is None or e.delivered_on + timedelta(days=RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS) > period_end):
            held_now += net

    # --- Released holds, adjustments, reserve, carried-in balance: the batch releases, adjusts,
    #     and pops these; the preview reads the same amounts without writing.
    released = sum(h.amount_cents for h in holds.releasable(seller.id, period_end))
    adjustments_cents = released + sum(a.amount_cents for a in adjustments if a.seller_id == seller.id)
    reserve_cents = apply_rate(gross_cents, seller.reserve_bp / 100) if seller.reserve_bp else 0
    carried_in_cents = rollover.balances.get(seller.id, 0)

    # --- Backup withholding: same as the batch (US sellers without a tax ID, on this period's
    #     net line amount, not carried balances or adjustments).
    if (seller_country or {}).get(seller.id, "US") == "US" and not seller.tax_id.strip():
        line_net = sum(line_nets) - held_now
        if line_net > 0:
            adjustments_cents -= apply_rate(line_net, BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP / 100)

    net = sum(line_nets) + adjustments_cents + carried_in_cents - held_now - reserve_cents

    # --- Status and amount: the batch's rules, in the batch's order.
    if seller.status in (SUSPENDED, CLOSED):
        return seller.status, 0                      # the batch skips these sellers; nothing is paid
    if net < 0 or (net < MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS and seller.status != CLOSING):
        return ROLLED_OVER, net                      # the batch would put this into the rollover; the preview leaves it
    if seller.payout_currency != settings.default_currency:
        if rates is None:
            return NO_RATES, net
        try:
            converted = rates.convert(net, settings.default_currency, seller.payout_currency, period_end)
        except RateUnavailable:
            return RATE_UNAVAILABLE, net
        net = converted - apply_rate(converted, FX_FEE_BP / 100)
    return DRAFT, net
```

```python
"""Payout preview: what the seller's next payout would look like before finance runs the weekly
batch.

build_payout_batch places new holds, releases due ones and takes the seller's carried balance
from the Rollover; a preview must not change anything, so the batch's per-seller math is
replayed against a copy of the HoldBook and a plain read of the rollover.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import copy
from datetime import date, timedelta

from shopkit.config import SETTINGS
from shopkit.payouts.batching import BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP, MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS, Rollover
from shopkit.payouts.holds import RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, HoldBook
from shopkit.payouts.models import CLOSING, CLOSED, DRAFT, ROLLED_OVER, SUSPENDED, Adjustment, Earning, Payout, PayoutLine, Seller
from shopkit.utils.numbers import apply_rate


def preview_payout(seller: Seller, earnings: list[Earning], adjustments: list[Adjustment],
                   period_start: date, period_end: date, holds: HoldBook, rollover: Rollover) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """The (status, net_cents) this seller's payout would get for [period_start, period_end]
    (inclusive), computed exactly the way build_payout_batch would treat it, without changing
    anything: no holds are placed or released and the carried balance is read, not taken.

    status is DRAFT or ROLLED_OVER when the batch would make a payout, the seller's status when
    the batch would skip the seller (suspended/closed), or "no rates" when the seller is paid in
    another currency and the preview has no rate table to convert with (the batch skips those
    sellers and carries the amount over). net_cents is 0 for skipped sellers."""
    if seller.status in (SUSPENDED, CLOSED):
        return seller.status, 0

    # --- input checks, the same as the batch: reject bad earnings, keep the first of a duplicate
    # (seller, order, sku) line (INC-2377)
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    own = []
    for e in earnings:
        if e.seller_id != seller.id:
            continue
        if e.gross_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents > e.gross_cents:
            continue
        key = (e.seller_id, e.order_id, e.sku)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        own.append(e)

    # Replay the batch's hold math on a copy: the real book keeps its holds, release dates and
    # released flags exactly as they were.
    book = copy.deepcopy(holds)
```

```python
"""Payout preview: what a seller's next payout would look like before finance runs the weekly
batch (batching.py).

The batch places new holds, releases due ones and takes the seller's carried balance from the
Rollover; a preview must not change anything, so the per-seller math is replayed against a copy
of the HoldBook and a plain read of the rollover.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import copy
from datetime import date, timedelta

from shopkit.config import SETTINGS
from shopkit.payouts.batching import BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP, MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS, Rollover
from shopkit.payouts.holds import RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, HoldBook
from shopkit.payouts.models import (CLOSING, CLOSED, DRAFT, ROLLED_OVER, SUSPENDED, Adjustment,
                                    Earning, Payout, PayoutLine, Seller)
from shopkit.utils.numbers import apply_rate


def preview_payout(seller: Seller, earnings: list[Earning], adjustments: list[Adjustment],
                   period_start: date, period_end: date, holds: HoldBook, rollover: Rollover) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """The (status, net_cents) this seller's payout would get for [period_start, period_end]
    (inclusive), treated exactly the way build_payout_batch would treat it, without changing
    anything: no holds are placed or released and the carried balance is read, not taken.

    status is DRAFT or ROLLED_OVER when the batch would make a payout, the seller's own status
    when the batch would skip the seller (suspended/closed), or "no rates" when the seller is
    paid in another currency and no rate table is available (the batch skips those sellers and
    carries the amount over). Skipped sellers get net_cents 0."""
    if seller.status in (SUSPENDED, CLOSED):
        return seller.status, 0

    # --- input checks, the same as the batch: reject invalid earnings, keep the first of a
    # duplicate (seller, order, sku) line (INC-2377)
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    own = []
    for e in earnings:
        if e.seller_id != seller.id:
            continue
        if e.gross_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents > e.gross_cents:
            continue
        key = (e.seller_id, e.order_id, e.sku)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        own.append(e)

    # Replay the hold math on a copy so release dates and the released flags are decided the way
    # the batch would decide them, while the real book stays exactly as it was.
    book = copy.deepcopy(holds)

    payout = Payout(f"preview_{seller.id}_{period_end:%Y%m%d}", seller.id, period_start, period_end,
                    seller.payout_currency)
    # same window as the batch: undelivered lines plus lines delivered within a year before the
    # period start up to period_end (INC-2291)
    in_period = [e for e in own
                 if e.delivered_on is None or period_start - timedelta(days=366) <= e.delivered_on <= period_end]

    # --- lines
    held_now = 0
    for e in sorted(in_period, key=lambda e: (e.order_id, e.sku)):
        commission = apply_rate(e.gross_cents, seller.commission_bp / 100)
```

   ```python
   """Read-only preview of a seller's next payout: what build_payout_batch would compute for one
   seller in a period, without changing anything (no holds placed or released, rollover read
   instead of taken)."""
   from __future__ import annotations

   from datetime import date, timedelta

   from shopkit.config import SETTINGS
   from shopkit.payouts.batching import BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP, MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS, Rollover
   from shopkit.payouts.holds import RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, HoldBook
   from shopkit.payouts.models import (CLOSED, CLOSING, DRAFT, ROLLED_OVER, SUSPENDED, Adjustment, Earning,
                                       Payout, PayoutLine, Seller)
   from shopkit.utils.numbers import apply_rate


   def preview_payout(seller: Seller, earnings: list[Earning], adjustments: list[Adjustment],
                      period_start: date, period_end: date, holds: HoldBook,
                      rollover: Rollover) -> tuple[str, int]:
       """What this seller's payout would be for [period_start, period_end] (inclusive), exactly as
       build_payout_batch would treat it: per-line commission and refunds, the net of lines still
       inside the return window held, holds released by period_end, adjustments, the reserve, the
       carried-in balance, backup withholding, and the minimum-payout and negative-balance rules.

       A preview changes nothing: holds are only counted, never placed or released, and the
       rollover balance is read, not taken. Returns (status, net_cents): a seller the batch skips
       (suspended or closed) is reported with that status and 0, and a foreign-currency draft is
       reported ROLLED_OVER with the net that would be carried forward, as the batch does when no
       rate table is available."""
       if seller.status in (SUSPENDED, CLOSED):
           return seller.status, 0

       # --- same input checks, dedupe and period filter as the batch (batching.py) -------------------
       in_period = []
       seen_now: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
       dry_run_dedupe = SETTINGS.flag("payout_dedupe_dry_run")
       for e in earnings:
           if e.seller_id != seller.id:
               continue
           if e.gross_cents < 0 or e.refunded_cents < 0:
               continue
           if e.refunded_cents > e.gross_cents:
               continue
           dup = (e.order_id, e.sku) in seen_now
           seen_now.add((e.order_id, e.sku))
           if dup and not dry_run_dedupe:
               continue
           if not (e.delivered_on is None or period_start - timedelta(days=366) <= e.delivered_on <= period_end):
               continue
           in_period.append(e)

       # --- lines: held amounts are counted, not placed ---------------------------------------------
       payout = Payout(f"po_{seller.id}_{period_end:%Y%m%d}", seller.id, period_start, period_end,
                       seller.payout_currency)
       held_now = 0
       for e in sorted(in_period, key=lambda e: (e.order_id, e.sku)):
           commission = apply_rate(e.gross_cents, seller.commission_bp / 100)
           net = e.gross_cents - commission - e.refunded_cents
           if e.refunded_cents and e.refunded_cents == e.gross_cents:
               # full refund: the commission is given back to the seller too (marketplace terms §7.2)
               net = 0
               commission = 0
           payout.lines.append(PayoutLine(e.order_id, e.gross_cents, commission, e.refunded_cents, net))
           within_window = e.delivered_on is None or e.delivered_on + timedelta(days=RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS) > period_end
           if within_window and net > 0:
               held_now += net
       payout.held_cents = held_now

       # --- released holds, adjustments, reserve and carried balance: read-only -----------------------
       released = sum(h.amount_cents for h in holds.releasable(seller.id, period_end))
       payout.adjustments_cents = sum(a.amount_cents for a in adjustments if a.seller_id == seller.id) + released
       if seller.reserve_bp:
           payout.reserve_cents = apply_rate(payout.gross_cents, seller.reserve_bp / 100)
       payout.carried_in_cents = rollover.balances.get(seller.id, 0)

       # --- backup withholding (a preview takes no seller_country, so US, as in the batch's default) --
       if not seller.tax_id.strip():
           line_net = sum(l.net_cents for l in payout.lines) - payout.held_cents
           if line_net > 0:
               payout.adjustments_cents -= apply_rate(line_net, BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP / 100)

       # --- minimum payout and negative balances --------------------------------------------------------
       net = payout.net_cents
       if net < 0:
           return ROLLED_OVER, net
       if net < MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS and seller.status != CLOSING:
           return ROLLED_OVER, net
       if seller.payout_currency != SETTINGS.default_currency:
           # the batch converts a foreign-currency draft with the period end's rate; without a rate
           # table it skips the payout and carries the net forward, so the preview reports the same
           return ROLLED_OVER, net
       return DRAFT, net
   ```

```python
"""Payout previews: show the seller what their next payout will look like before finance runs the
weekly batch.

Computes the same numbers build_payout_batch does for one seller (commission, return-window holds,
adjustments, reserves, carried balances, minimum payout, backup withholding, FX) and reports the
status the batch would record. A preview changes nothing: it counts the holds that would be placed
but never calls HoldBook.place/release, reads the carried balance but never calls Rollover.take,
and creates no Payout — so the real batch sees the same holds and balances."""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, timedelta

from shopkit.config import SETTINGS, Settings
from shopkit.payouts.batching import BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP, FX_FEE_BP, MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS, Rollover, _commission
from shopkit.payouts.holds import RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, HoldBook
from shopkit.payouts.models import (CLOSED, CLOSING, DRAFT, ROLLED_OVER, SUSPENDED, Adjustment,
                                    Earning, Seller)
from shopkit.pricing.currency import RateTable, RateUnavailable
from shopkit.utils.numbers import apply_rate

NO_RATES = "no rates"
RATE_UNAVAILABLE = "rate unavailable"


def preview_payout(seller: Seller, earnings: list[Earning], adjustments: list[Adjustment],
                   period_start: date, period_end: date, holds: HoldBook, rollover: Rollover,
                   rates: RateTable | None = None, settings: Settings = SETTINGS,
                   paid_lines: set[tuple[str, str, str]] | None = None,
                   seller_country: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """What the weekly batch would pay `seller` for [period_start, period_end] (both ends inclusive).

    Returns (status, net_cents): the status the batch would record for the payout (DRAFT,
    ROLLED_OVER, the skip reason "no rates" / "rate unavailable", or the seller's own status when
    suspended/closed) and the net payout in the seller's payout currency. Skipped and
    suspended/closed sellers get 0; ROLLED_OVER gets the balance the batch would carry forward.

    `holds` and `rollover` are read the way the batch reads them (which holds are releasable at
    period_end, which carried balance there is) but never written, so a preview leaves both exactly
    as they were and the real batch still processes them.

    The optional arguments mirror the batch: `rates` is required when the seller is paid in a
    currency other than the shop's, `paid_lines` are (seller, order, sku) lines already paid in an
    earlier batch, and `seller_country` drives backup withholding (US sellers without a tax ID).
    """
    # --- Input checks: same rules as the batch (negative or over-refunded lines don't become payout lines) ---
    valid = [e for e in earnings
             if e.seller_id == seller.id and e.gross_cents >= 0 and e.refunded_cents >= 0
             and e.refunded_cents <= e.gross_cents]

    # --- Deduplication, same as the batch (INC-2377): already-paid lines and duplicates in this
    #     period are not paid again. The dry-run flag is an incident switch, not the batch's
    #     behaviour, so it does not apply here.
    paid_lines = paid_lines if paid_lines is not None else frozenset()
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    deduped = []
    for e in valid:
        key = (e.seller_id, e.order_id, e.sku)
        if key in paid_lines or key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        deduped.append(e)

    in_period = [e for e in deduped
                 if e.delivered_on is None or period_start - timedelta(days=366) <= e.delivered_on <= period_end]

    # --- Lines: same commission, refund, and hold rules as the batch. The batch calls holds.place
    #     here; the preview only counts what would be held, so the book stays intact.
    gross_cents = 0
    line_nets: list[int] = []
    held_now = 0
    for e in sorted(in_period, key=lambda e: (e.order_id, e.sku)):
        commission = _commission(e.gross_cents, seller.commission_bp)
        net = e.gross_cents - commission - e.refunded_cents
        if e.refunded_cents and e.refunded_cents == e.gross_cents:
            # Fully refunded orders return the commission to the seller too (marketplace terms §7.2)
            net = 0
            commission = 0
        gross_cents += e.gross_cents
        line_nets.append(net)
        if net > 0 and (e.delivered_on is None or e.delivered_on + timedelta(days=RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS) > period_end):
            held_now += net

    # --- Released holds, adjustments, reserve, carried-in balance: the batch releases, adjusts,
    #     and pops these; the preview reads the same amounts without writing.
    released = sum(h.amount_cents for h in holds.releasable(seller.id, period_end))
    adjustments_cents = released + sum(a.amount_cents for a in adjustments if a.seller_id == seller.id)
    reserve_cents = apply_rate(gross_cents, seller.reserve_bp / 100) if seller.reserve_bp else 0
    carried_in_cents = rollover.balances.get(seller.id, 0)

    # --- Backup withholding: same as the batch (US sellers without a tax ID, on this period's
    #     net line amount, not carried balances or adjustments).
    if (seller_country or {}).get(seller.id, "US") == "US" and not seller.tax_id.strip():
        line_net = sum(line_nets) - held_now
        if line_net > 0:
            adjustments_cents -= apply_rate(line_net, BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP / 100)

    net = sum(line_nets) + adjustments_cents + carried_in_cents - held_now - reserve_cents

    # --- Status and amount: the batch's rules, in the batch's order.
    if seller.status in (SUSPENDED, CLOSED):
        return seller.status, 0                      # the batch skips these sellers; nothing is paid
    if net < 0 or (net < MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS and seller.status != CLOSING):
        return ROLLED_OVER, net                      # the batch would put this into the rollover; the preview leaves it
    if seller.payout_currency != settings.default_currency:
        if rates is None:
            return NO_RATES, net
        try:
            converted = rates.convert(net, settings.default_currency, seller.payout_currency, period_end)
        except RateUnavailable:
            return RATE_UNAVAILABLE, net
        net = converted - apply_rate(converted, FX_FEE_BP / 100)
    return DRAFT, net
```

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, timedelta

from shopkit.config import SETTINGS, Settings
from shopkit.payouts.batching import BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP, FX_FEE_BP, MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS, Rollover, _commission
from shopkit.payouts.holds import RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS, HoldBook
from shopkit.payouts.models import (CLOSED, CLOSING, DRAFT, ROLLED_OVER, SUSPENDED, Adjustment,
                                    Earning, Seller)
from shopkit.pricing.currency import RateTable, RateUnavailable
from shopkit.utils.numbers import apply_rate


def preview_payout(seller: Seller, earnings: list[Earning], adjustments: list[Adjustment],
                   period_start: date, period_end: date, holds: HoldBook, rollover: Rollover,
                   rates: RateTable | None = None, settings: Settings = SETTINGS,
                   paid_lines: set[tuple[str, str, str]] | None = None,
                   seller_country: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """What the weekly batch would pay `seller` for [period_start, period_end] (inclusive).

    Returns (status, net_cents): the status the batch would record for the payout (DRAFT,
    ROLLED_OVER, the skip reason "no rates" / "rate unavailable", or the seller's own status when
    suspended/closed) and the net amount in the seller's payout currency. Suspended/closed and
    skipped sellers get 0 (the batch pays them nothing); ROLLED_OVER gets the balance the batch
    would carry forward.

    `holds` and `rollover` are read the way the batch reads them — which holds are releasable at
    period_end, which carried balance there is — but never written, so a preview leaves both
    exactly as they were and the real batch still processes them.

    The optional arguments mirror the batch: `rates` is required when the seller is paid in a
    currency other than the shop's, `paid_lines` are (seller, order, sku) lines already paid in an
    earlier batch, and `seller_country` drives backup withholding (US sellers without a tax id).
    """
    # --- input checks: the batch's rules (negative or over-refunded lines do not become payout lines) ---
    valid = [e for e in earnings
             if e.seller_id == seller.id and e.gross_cents >= 0 and e.refunded_cents >= 0
             and e.refunded_cents <= e.gross_cents]

    # --- dedupe, same as the batch (INC-2377): already-paid lines and duplicates in this period
    # are not paid twice. The dry-run flag is an incident switch, not the batch's behaviour.
    paid_lines = paid_lines if paid_lines is not None else frozenset()
    seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    deduped = []
    for e in valid:
        key = (e.seller_id, e.order_id, e.sku)
        if key in paid_lines or key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        deduped.append(e)

    in_period = [e for e in deduped
                 if e.delivered_on is None or period_start - timedelta(days=366) <= e.delivered_on <= period_end]

    # --- lines: the batch's commission, refund and hold rules. The batch calls holds.place here;
    # the preview only counts what would be held, so the book stays intact.
    gross_cents = 0
    line_nets: list[int] = []
    held_now = 0
    for e in sorted(in_period, key=lambda e: (e.order_id, e.sku)):
        commission = 0
        net = e.gross_cents - commission - e.refunded_cents
        if e.refunded_cents and e.refunded_cents == e.gross_cents:
            # full refund: the commission is given back to the seller too (marketplace terms §7.2)
            net = 0
            commission = 0
        gross_cents += e.gross_cents
        line_nets.append(net)
        if net > 0 and (e.delivered_on is None or e.delivered_on + timedelta(days=RETURN_WINDOW_DAYS) > period_end):
            held_now += net

    # --- released holds, adjustments, reserve, carried balance: the batch releases, adjusts and
    # pops these; the preview reads the same amounts without writing.
    released = sum(h.amount_cents for h in holds.releasable(seller.id, period_end))
    adjustments_cents = released + sum(a.amount_cents for a in adjustments if a.seller_id == seller.id)
    reserve_cents = apply_rate(gross_cents, seller.reserve_bp / 100) if seller.reserve_bp else 0
    carried_in_cents = rollover.balances.get(seller.id, 0)

    # --- backup withholding: as in the batch, US sellers without a tax id, on the period's net
    # line amounts (not of carried balances or adjustments).
    if (seller_country or {}).get(seller.id, "US") == "US" and not seller.tax_id.strip():
        line_net = sum(line_nets) - held_now
        if line_net > 0:
            adjustments_cents -= apply_rate(line_net, BACKUP_WITHHOLDING_BP / 100)

    net = sum(line_nets) + adjustments_cents + carried_in_cents - held_now - reserve_cents

    # --- status and amount: the batch's rules, in the batch's order.
    if seller.status in (SUSPENDED, CLOSED):
        return seller.status, 0                    # the batch skips these sellers; nothing is paid
    if net < 0:
        return ROLLED_OVER, net                    # never "paid"; the batch would carry it forward
    if net < MIN_PAYOUT_CENTS and seller.status != CLOSING:
        return ROLLED_OVER, net                    # below the bank minimum; the batch would carry it forward
    if seller.payout_currency != settings.default_currency:
        if rates is None:
            return "no rates", net
        try:
            converted = rates.convert(net, settings.default_currency, seller.payout_currency, period_end)
        except RateUnavailable:
            return "rate unavailable", net
        net = converted - apply_rate(converted, FX_FEE_BP / 100)
    return DRAFT, net
